_about: What it means for you, per topic: a 30-second check (three questions; the answer in 'flag' shows its fix) and what to watch (dated where a real date exists). Calls are linked by id from research/calls.json. Evergreen; review the watch list every refresh. No scores, no fear-bait: each flagged answer gets one concrete fix.

check.q: Do your kids use an AI chatbot or a 'companion' app?
check.fix: Open the app together and look at its age and companion settings. Ask what they talk to it about, without judgment.
link: A parent's guide to AI companions

check.q: Are photos of your kids public on social media?
check.fix: Switch those accounts to private or limit who can see the photos; public images are what deepfake abusers use.
link: What to do if it happens

check.q: Has your family agreed a safe word for emergency calls?
check.fix: Pick one tonight. A cloned voice can't answer a question only your family knows.

watch.text: Google's deadline to answer Senators Hawley and Blumenthal on AI switched on by default for students

check.q: Is there a recording of your voice online (videos, a voicemail greeting, podcasts)?
check.fix: Assume your voice can be cloned. Tell family that a panicked call asking for money gets a call-back on a number they already have.
link: A loved one calls in a panic: what to do

check.q: Would you move money if a relative called in a panic and asked?
check.fix: Make a rule now: no money moves on an incoming call or video. Hang up and call back.
link: Is this a scam? Check it

check.q: Have you given an app or AI agent your bank login?
check.fix: Revoke it in your bank's settings and change the password; banks are restricting third-party agents found inside accounts.

check.q: Do you paste work documents into AI tools your employer hasn't approved?
check.fix: Stop pasting customer, patient or HR data into unapproved tools. A hospital worker on our record exposed 3,182 patients that way this month.

check.q: Is most of your job writing, customer support, data entry or first-pass analysis?
check.fix: See how your job is graded, task by task, and which tasks AI has actually taken over so far.

check.q: Have you applied for jobs through online application systems this year?
check.fix: Software often screens applications before a person sees them. Ask employers whether AI screens applicants, and keep copies of what you submit.

watch.text: Workday hiring-bias case: hearing on whether applicants can sue as a class

check.q: Is your health plan Medicare Advantage, or one that needs approval before care?
check.fix: If care is denied, ask in writing whether a clinician reviewed it and how the decision was made, then appeal. You have a right to appeal a denial.

check.q: Do you ask AI chatbots about symptoms or medicines?
check.fix: Use the answer as a list of questions for a clinician, not a diagnosis; chatbots can state wrong doses and conditions confidently.

check.q: Has your hospital or clinic told you how it uses AI on your records?
check.fix: Ask. You can request to know who your records were shared with; hospital staff on our record uploaded patient files to unapproved AI.

watch.text: Families v. UnitedHealth: a court ordered the insurer to show how its nH Predict tool works

check.q: Is a data centre planned or being built near you?
check.fix: Find the local zoning or utility hearing and ask who pays for the new power lines and plants; residents can comment in public.
link: AI near you: the local fights

check.q: Has your electric utility asked to raise rates this year?
check.fix: Look up the rate case at your state utility commission and ask whether data centres pay for the growth they cause. Comments from customers go on the record.

check.q: Do you know which state agency approves your power rates?
check.fix: It is usually the public utility (or public service) commission. Its website lists open rate cases and how to comment.

watch.text: Arizona: the attorney general wants an audit of whether homes paid data-centre-driven fuel costs; APS asks for a 14% to 16% residential rise
Oregon, Ohio votes on Issue 25, a ban on data centers of 25 megawatts or more

check.q: Does your website run on PHP (WordPress, Drupal, Laravel and many others do)?
check.fix: Ask your host or developer to confirm it runs a PHP release fixed on or after Oct 21, 2026.

check.q: Do plugins, outside tools or AI agents hold keys to your site or systems?
check.fix: List them, remove the ones you don't use, and rotate the keys of the rest; this month's breaches went through third-party software.

check.q: Does your robots.txt block AI training crawlers?
check.fix: Build one that names the crawlers that scrape for AI.

watch.text: Federal deadline for US agencies to fix the two PHP flaws CISA lists as used in attacks

check.q: Do you get most election news from short videos on social media?
check.fix: Before sharing a shocking clip, check whether a major outlet or the campaign itself has confirmed it.
link: Is this video real? How to check

check.q: Have you seen a political ad this year that you weren't sure was real?
check.fix: Look for the disclosure line; in states that require labels, a study found only 29% of AI ads carried one. Report unlabelled ones to your state election office.
link: Every AI fake in the midterms

check.q: Do you know where to check your polling place and hours officially?
check.fix: Use your state or county election office's own site, not a link from a message or post. Fake voting information is a known AI use.
